chunks: And from Khalaf bin al-Walid al-Lu'lu'i, from Israel, from Sammak, who said: I heard Jabir bin Samra saying: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) saying: After him - or those after him - twelve leaders will arise.
Then he spoke a word that I did not understand, so I asked the people what he had said? They said: He said: All of them are from Quraysh.
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the number and lineage of his successors?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded by al-Nu'mani in *Kitab al-Ghayba*, serves as a foundational Sunni-Shia consensus text (muttafaq 'alayh) regarding the number and tribal origin of the twelve Imams. While Sunni tradition often identifies these as the first twelve Caliphs, Shia scholarship interprets 'amir' here as divinely appointed Imams, specifically linking the 'from Quraysh' criterion to the twelve specific figures culminating in Imam al-Mahdi (AJ).

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (12) Khalaf bin al-Waleed al-Lu’lu’iy narrated from Sammak that Jabir bin Samra had said: “I heard the Prophet (S) saying that there would be twelve emirs after him.
Then he said something that I could not understand. I asked some people what he had said. They told me that he had said: “All of them are from Quraysh.”
